prompt:
Generated with Codex CLI image_generation (sheet logo-v2, attempt 2), ink extracted to alpha by assets/scripts/extract.mjs, jug mark cropped out. Prompt:
STYLE — applies to everything in this image:
- It must look like a real flatbed scan of an actual hand-made drawing on plain white paper, made by Norma, a 70-year-old retired Argentine art teacher ("profesora de plástica") who now makes ceramics. Her hand is experienced and confident, but she works fast and doesn't fuss: lines are loose and a little imperfect.
- Medium: black India ink applied with a worn round watercolor brush. Visible pressure variation along each stroke (thick to thin), dry-brush breakup where the brush ran out of ink, slightly ragged edges, a few tiny ink specks, stroke ends that taper or end in a small blob, shapes that don't perfectly close.
- Pure black ink only. No grey wash, no colour, no shading, no hatching.
- Background: perfectly flat pure white (#FFFFFF). No paper texture, no shadows, no vignette, no scanner edges, no border, nothing else on the page, so the ink can be extracted cleanly.
- Avoid anything that looks digital: no vector-perfect curves, no symmetry, no font-like lettering, no glossy, 3D or neon effects, no extra words, no signature, no watermark, no mockup, no hands, no brush or ink bottle in the picture.

Portrait image, 1024x1536.

SUBJECT: a lettering practice sheet. Three separate attempts of the same small logo, stacked vertically with a lot of white space between them, as if she tried it three times on the same page. The attempts must genuinely differ from each other: different sizes, slightly different positions on the page, one a bit tilted, one more compressed. Each attempt has:
- the word "Norma" written in clear, very legible lowercase print handwriting: separate letters, NOT joined cursive (it must be easy to read for older people);
- directly under it, about one third of the size and with a thinner line (written with just the tip of the brush), the word "cerámica" (with the accent on the é) in loose hand-printed lowercase letters;
- to the left of "Norma", a tiny drawing of a round-bellied clay jug with a small handle, made with just 3 to 5 brush strokes.

Make it feel genuinely human, not like a brush font:
- each letter a slightly different height and slant, the baseline wobbles, spacing between letters is uneven;
- the brush is loaded with ink at the start of each stroke (dark, slightly blobby) and runs dry towards the end (broken, scratchy), so every stroke has its own texture instead of the same rough edge everywhere;
- one or two places where strokes overlap because she lifted the brush and started again.

Spell exactly "Norma" and "cerámica". No other text anywhere.
